verses.text: Abimelech son of Jerub-Baal went to Shechem, to his mother’s brothers and her whole family, and pitched them an idea. 🏙️
‘Ask all Shechem’s leaders this: What works better for you—seventy of Jerub-Baal’s sons ruling you, or just one? Remember, I’m your own flesh and blood.’ 🗣️
His mother’s brothers passed the message around Shechem. The people leaned toward Abimelech because, as they said, ‘He’s family.’ 🤝
They gave him seventy pieces of silver from Baal-Berith’s temple. Abimelech used it to hire reckless troublemakers who followed him. 💰
He went to his father’s home in Ophrah and killed his seventy brothers, Jerub-Baal’s sons, on one stone. But the youngest, Jotham, hid and survived. ⚠️
Then Shechem’s leaders and the whole house of Millo gathered and made Abimelech king beside the oak at Shechem’s pillar. 👑
When Jotham heard, he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim, raised his voice, and called out: ‘Shechem’s leaders, listen up, so God may listen to you too! 📣
‘One day the trees went to choose a king. They asked the olive tree, “Rule over us.” 🌳
‘But the olive tree said, “Should I stop making my oil, which honors God and people, just to sway above the other trees?” 🫒
‘Then the trees asked the fig tree, “Come rule over us.” 🌳
‘The fig tree said, “Should I give up my sweetness and good fruit just to sway above the trees?” 🍈
‘Then the trees asked the grapevine, “Come rule over us.” 🌳
‘The vine said, “Should I give up my wine that cheers God and people just to sway above the trees?” 🍇
‘Finally, all the trees asked the thornbush, “Come rule over us.” 🌵
‘The thornbush told them, “If you’re honestly anointing me king, come take shelter in my shade. If not, let fire come out from me and burn Lebanon’s cedars!” 🔥
‘So tell me: did you make Abimelech king fairly and honorably? Did you treat Jerub-Baal and his family right? ⚖️
‘My father fought for you, risked his life, and rescued you from Midian. 🛡️

‘But today you turned against my father’s family and killed his seventy sons on one stone. Then you made Abimelech king over Shechem, even though he’s the son of my father’s servant woman—just because he’s your relative. 💔
‘If you truly acted fairly toward Jerub-Baal and his family, then celebrate Abimelech—and let him celebrate you too. 🎉
‘But if you didn’t, may fire come from Abimelech and burn Shechem’s leaders and the house of Millo; and may fire come from Shechem and Millo and burn Abimelech.’ 🔥
Then Jotham ran off to Beer and lived there, hiding from his brother Abimelech. 🏃
Abimelech ruled over Israel for three years. ⏳
Then God set hostility between Abimelech and Shechem’s leaders, and they betrayed him. ⚡
That happened so the violence against Jerub-Baal’s seventy sons would come back on Abimelech, their brother who killed them, and on Shechem’s leaders who backed him. ⚖️
Shechem’s leaders set ambushes on the mountain tops and robbed everyone passing by. Abimelech heard about it. 🏔️
Then Gaal son of Ebed arrived in Shechem with his brothers, and the people put their trust in him. 👥
They went out to the fields, picked grapes, stomped them, threw a party, then went into their god’s temple to eat and drink—and trash-talk Abimelech. 🍇

Gaal son of Ebed said, ‘Who even is Abimelech? Why should Shechem answer to him? Isn’t he Jerub-Baal’s son, with Zebul as his deputy? Serve Hamor’s family—the original Shechem crew. Why should we serve Abimelech? 🗣️
‘If these people were under my command, I’d remove Abimelech.’ Then he sent him a challenge: ‘Build your army up and come face me!’ 💪
Zebul, the city’s governor, heard Gaal son of Ebed and got furious. 😠
He secretly sent messengers to Abimelech: ‘Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers are here in Shechem, stirring the city against you. 🤫
‘So tonight, you and your people, move in and hide in the fields. 🌙
‘At sunrise, get up early and rush the city. When Gaal and his people come out against you, handle it however you see the opening.’ ⚔️
Abimelech and his men got up during the night and set four groups of fighters in ambush around Shechem. 🌃
Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the city gate. Abimelech and his men rose from their hiding spots. 👀
Gaal saw them and told Zebul, ‘Look, people are coming down from the mountain tops!’ Zebul said, ‘Those are just mountain shadows looking like people.’ 🏔️
Gaal looked again: ‘No, people are coming down from the middle of the land, and one group is coming along the Diviners’ Oak road.’ 👁️
Zebul said, ‘Where’s that big talk now? You said, “Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?” Aren’t these the people you disrespected? Go out and fight them!’ 🗯️
Gaal led Shechem’s men out to fight Abimelech. ⚔️
Abimelech chased Gaal, who ran away. Many were wounded and fell all the way to the city gate. 🏃
Abimelech stayed in Arumah, while Zebul drove Gaal and his brothers out so they couldn’t live in Shechem anymore. 🚪
The next day the people went out into the fields, and someone told Abimelech. 🌅
He split his people into three groups and hid them in the fields. When he saw the townspeople coming out, he attacked them. ⚔️
Abimelech and his group rushed to the city gate and held it. The other two groups attacked everyone out in the fields. 🛡️
Abimelech fought the city all day, captured it, killed its people, smashed the city, and scattered salt over the ground. ⚠️
When the leaders in Shechem’s tower heard, they took refuge inside El-Berith’s temple fortress. 🏰
Abimelech was told that all the tower’s leaders had gathered there. 📣
He climbed Mount Zalmon with his men, cut a tree branch with an axe, hoisted it onto his shoulder, and told them, ‘Quick—do what you just saw me do!’ 🪓
So each man cut a branch too. They followed Abimelech, piled the branches against the stronghold, and set it on fire. Around a thousand men and women in the tower died. 🔥
Then Abimelech went to Thebez, camped against it, and captured the city. 🏙️
But there was a fortified tower inside the city. All the men and women ran there, locked themselves in, and went up to its roof. 🏰
Abimelech came to attack the tower and moved up to its entrance to burn it. 🔥
Then a woman dropped an upper millstone onto Abimelech’s head and cracked his skull. ⚠️
He quickly called his young armor-bearer: ‘Draw your sword and kill me, so nobody can say, “A woman killed him.”’ His armor-bearer stabbed him, and he died. 🗡️
When Israel’s men saw Abimelech was dead, each one went home. 🏠
That’s how God paid Abimelech back for the evil he did to his father by killing his seventy brothers. ⚖️
God also paid Shechem’s leaders back for all their evil, and Jotham son of Jerub-Baal’s curse came down on them. ⚖️
